title: Long Cycles in 2-Connected Tough Graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a graph. The circumference of $G$, denoted by $cir(G)$, is the length of a longest cycle in $G$, or zero if $G$ is acyclic. In 1993, Broersma, van den Heuvel, Jung, and Veldman conjectured that, for every $t>0$, there is a constant $A=A(t)>0$ such that every 2-connected $t$-tough graph of order $n$ has circumference at least $A\log n$; the conjecture is recorded as Conjecture~2 in the 2006 survey on toughness by Bauer, Broersma, and Schmeichel.
